subject: ventures/restaurant-pos-menu-mix-analyzer
professional: a restaurant consultant / F&B controller who runs menu-engineering reviews from POS product-mix reports; first checks: is the margin bar the weighted average CM (total CM / total plates), is the popularity bar 70% of 1/n, are refunds, voids, comps and modifiers handled, where do plate costs come from, and are items only compared with items they compete with (same menu category)

evidence.correctness: Recomputed with my own Python script (scratchpad mm/indep.py, written from the Kasavana & Smith method, not from calc.mjs) on the built-in sample: 14 items, 2,303 plates, threshold 5.000%, weighted avg CM 7.2528, total CM 16,703.31 and all 14 classes match the tool exactly. Hand-checked a Toast-style 8-entree file with a Food Cost % column and a 'Total' row: threshold 8.75%, avg CM 15.12 (sales 2,229 - cost 717.00 over 100 plates), classes as hand-derived. Hand-checked the Plowhorse price rise for House Fries (5.00 -> 5.25, 520 -> 504.4 plates: +64.48, break-even loss 1 - 3.95/4.20 = 5.952%) and an exact-70% boundary item (7 of 100 plates on 10 items: popular). Semicolon/decimal-comma file with a preamble and a UTF-16 tab file read correctly. One input-handling defect: a percent cost column written as a fraction (0.38) is read as 0.38% with no warning, flipping classes.
evidence.completeness: README/page features checked end to end via calc.mjs on real-shaped files: alias header matching (Menu Item/Menu Group/Item Qty/Net Amount resolved), preamble rows skipped, total row skipped, voided and '+ modifier' rows skipped and reported, refunds netted, duplicates merged, cost precedence export > list > default with placeholder flag, zero-cost and cost-above-price flags, Plowhorse rise with break-even loss, cut/re-promote lists, category rollup that reconciles to the totals (352 = 352 sales, 239.36 = 239.36 CM), CSV download with formula neutralising, summary text, UTF-16 and semicolon files. All worked; no TODOs or stubs. Linked sibling tools exist (menu-engineering-calculator, production-mix-optimizer, pour-cost-calculator).
evidence.verification: node --test '*.test.mjs' (and plain node --test as the README says) in the subject dir: 45 tests, 45 pass, ~0.1 s, Node 22.23.5. Six seeded mutants via quality_mutate.py: popularity factor 0.7->0.75, weighted->simple average CM, >= -> > at the popularity boundary, volume loss dropped from the price rise, and percent cost applied to total sales instead of price were all caught; dividing the export cost sum by net qty instead of costed qty (differs only when a refund row meets an export cost column) survived.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (370 lines, pure functions, no DOM), index.html inline script, usage.mjs, calc.test.mjs, page.test.mjs. Clean separation, escaped HTML output, CSV injection guarded, storage access wrapped. Minor: usedNames.add is called twice for listed items (calc.mjs:202 and 204); detectDecimalComma is defined after the sample and only used by the page; index.html render lines run to 400+ characters.
evidence.claims: Checked: weighted average margin and 70% rule (calc.mjs:217-224), refunds netted / voids and modifiers skipped / duplicates merged (calc.mjs:127-129, 178-190), cost precedence and placeholder flag (calc.mjs:200-203, 261), zero-cost flag (263), 'reconciles' (verified numerically), 'never uploaded' (page.test.mjs asserts no network; no fetch in calc.mjs or the page), usage counted only in localStorage, DNT/GPC honoured and the opt-out button deletes the counts (usage.mjs setUsageOptOut removes KEY). Unverified-alias limitation stated on README and page. Disclaimer, no-warranty and non-affiliation footer present. Served copy (node platform/pages/served-copy.mjs) has no placeholder or retired origin left; the github.io links in source llms.txt are rewritten at deploy (source-only).
evidence.fitness: Walked the owner's job: export item sales, paste costs, read classes, price a rise. Works on Toast/Square-shaped headers I built, but no real Toast, Square or Clover export has ever been read (README says so), Square-style variation rows of one item at different prices merge into one averaged item, and the single whole-menu matrix ranks fries and sparkling water against a ribeye, so the cut/re-promote list a consultant would hand a chef needs a per-category re-run the tool does not offer (the owner must split the file by hand).
evidence.domain: Kasavana & Smith (1982) arithmetic is right: CM bar = weighted average CM, popularity bar = 70% x (1/n), four classes, boundaries inclusive. Departure: the matrix is computed once across every category in the file (calc.mjs:219, 214-218); menu-engineering practice analyses items that compete with each other (a menu category such as entrees), and mixing sides, drinks, desserts and mains shifts both bars (sample: House Fries, Cold Brew and Sparkling Water become the Plowhorses whose prices it proposes raising, while every dessert is a Dog). The category rollup shows totals but no per-category classes. Default 32% food cost is a flagged placeholder, not a cited benchmark.

mutations.change: weighted avgCm (totalCm / totalUnits) -> simple mean of item CMs
mixPct >= popThreshold - EPS -> mixPct > popThreshold + EPS
unitCost = costSum / costQty -> costSum / qty (net of refunds)
percent cost x price -> percent cost x row sales

defects.what: One menu-engineering matrix across every category in the file: sides, drinks and desserts are ranked against mains, which moves both the popularity and the margin bar. On the sample the proposed Plowhorse price rises land on House Fries, Cold Brew and Sparkling Water and every dessert is a Dog. Practice is to analyse competing items (a category); the category rollup has no per-category classes and there is no option to classify within category

A Food Cost % column holding fractions (0.38) is read as 0.38%, giving near-zero plate costs and flipped classes with no warning (Pork Chop Plowhorse->Star, Roast Chicken Star->Plowhorse on an 8-entree file). Small safe fix: when every non-blank cost-% value is <= 1, treat them as fractions or raise a finding

Column aliases have never been checked against a real Toast, Square or Clover export (stated on the page); Square-style variation rows of one item at different price points merge into one averaged item, so a Small/Large latte is classified as one dish
No test covers a refund row on an item whose export carries a cost column: changing the cost-weighting denominator from costed quantity to net quantity leaves all 45 tests green
usedNames.add(normName(m.name)) runs twice for a listed item (inside the list branch and again unconditionally)

verdict: The Kasavana & Smith arithmetic is right: my independent script reproduces all 14 classes, the 5.00% popularity bar, the 7.2528 weighted average CM and the 16,703.31 total CM on the sample, and hand checks of a Toast-style entree file, an exact-70% boundary and the Plowhorse price rise (+64.48, break-even 5.95%) all match. 45 tests pass and catch 5 of 6 seeded bugs; claims, privacy and disclaimer are backed. It meets the bar, but a consultant would not hand its cut/re-price list to a chef as is: it builds one matrix across mains, sides, drinks and desserts (so the price rises land on fries and sparkling water), a fractional cost-% column is silently read 100x too small, and no real POS export has been read yet.
